[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "title": "Geometric Foundations and Iterative Nature of the Simplex Method",
    "scope": "Explains the geometric philosophy of the simplex method as an edge-following algorithm on convex polyhedra. Covers starting at the coordinate origin where all original decision variables are zero, traversing adjacent extreme points (vertices) along boundary edges without cutting through the feasible interior, and adjusting variables one at a time based on maximal rate of improvement.",
    "key_points": [
      "Standard initialization at the origin extreme point where nonbasic decision variables satisfy $x_j = 0$ for all $j$",
      "Movement restricted strictly along the 1-dimensional edges of the feasible polytope connecting adjacent corner points (vertices)",
      "Prohibition of interior traversal: the algorithm cannot take a direct interior path from initial to optimal vertex",
      "One-variable-at-a-time improvement strategy: selecting the candidate variable possessing the highest marginal rate of improvement (largest positive gradient coefficient in $z$)",
      "Correspondence between geometric corner points and algebraic iterations of the simplex algorithm"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "title": "Standard LP Augmentation and Initial Simplex Tableau Construction",
    "scope": "Details the algebraic preparation required to initialize the tabular simplex method. Teaches the conversion of linear inequality constraints into equality form using non-negative slack variables, rewriting the objective function in homogeneous zero-sum form, and structuring the full simplex tableau with basic and nonbasic variable partitions.",
    "key_points": [
      "Transformation of $\\le$ inequality constraints into equalities via non-negative slack variables $s_i \\ge 0$",
      "Algebraic reformulation of the objective equation into homogeneous form: $z - \\sum c_j x_j - \\sum 0 s_i = 0$",
      "Partitioning of the $n$ variables into $m$ basic variables (initially slacks) and $n-m$ nonbasic variables set to zero",
      "Canonical layout of the simplex tableau: basic variable column, $z$-column, variable coefficient matrix, and Right-Hand-Side (RHS) Solution column",
      "Identification of the initial basic feasible solution (BFS) directly readable from the RHS solution column"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "title": "The Simplex Optimality Condition and Entering Variable Selection",
    "scope": "Formulates the test for optimality and the mathematical mechanism for choosing the entering variable. Explains how the $z$-row coefficients (reduced costs) represent potential improvement in the objective value and establishes the selection rule for maximization versus minimization problems.",
    "key_points": [
      "Interpretation of $z$-row coefficients: negative coefficients indicate nonbasic variables whose increase will raise the value of $z$",
      "Simplex Optimality Condition for maximization: the entering variable is the nonbasic variable with the most negative coefficient in the objective row ($z$-row)",
      "Simplex Optimality Condition for minimization: the entering variable is the nonbasic variable with the most positive coefficient in the $z$-row",
      "Designation of the entering variable's column as the pivot column",
      "Termination criterion: optimality is achieved when all reduced cost coefficients in the $z$-row are non-negative (for maximization) or non-positive (for minimization)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "title": "The Simplex Feasibility Condition and the Minimum Ratio Test",
    "scope": "Teaches the mathematical derivation and geometric justification of the minimum ratio test used to select the leaving variable. Shows how positive constraint coefficients bound the increase of the entering variable and prevents violation of non-negativity.",
    "key_points": [
      "Simplex Feasibility Condition: identification of the basic variable that hits zero first as the entering variable increases",
      "Minimum ratio calculation: $\\theta^* = \\min_i \\{ \\text{Solution}_i / a_{ik} \\mid a_{ik} > 0 \\}$, where $k$ denotes the pivot column",
      "Strict restriction to strictly positive denominators: non-positive coefficients ($a_{ik} \\le 0$) do not constrain variable growth and are ignored",
      "Geometric interpretation: ratios correspond exactly to the intercepts of active constraint hyperplanes with the entering variable axis",
      "Selection of the pivot row based on the minimum ratio and identification of the leaving variable"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "title": "Gauss-Jordan Row Operations and Tableau Pivoting Mechanics",
    "scope": "Formulates the algebraic machinery for updating the simplex tableau across iterations. Details the identification of the pivot element and the step-by-step application of elementary row operations to transition from one basic feasible solution to an adjacent one.",
    "key_points": [
      "Definition of the pivot element located at the intersection of the pivot row and pivot column",
      "Basis update: replacement of the leaving variable by the entering variable in the Basic column",
      "Pivot row normalization: $\\text{New pivot row} = \\text{Current pivot row} / \\text{Pivot element}$",
      "Elimination on all non-pivot rows (including the $z$-row): $\\text{New row} = \\text{Current row} - (\\text{Pivot column coefficient}) \\times (\\text{New pivot row})$",
      "Preservation of canonical unit-vector form for all basic variables across the updated tableau"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "title": "Algorithmic Execution and Multi-Iteration Simplex Walkthrough",
    "scope": "Provides a comprehensive, end-to-end trace of multi-iteration tableau progression using the Tatar-Paint production model. Tracks numerical transitions from the origin BFS through intermediate basic solutions to the final global optimum, verifying both arithmetic and geometric convergence.",
    "key_points": [
      "Iteration 1 pivot: entering $x_1$, leaving $s_1$ with pivot element 6, yielding objective value $z = 20$",
      "Iteration 1 tableau evaluation: remaining negative coefficient ($-2/3$ under $x_2$) confirming non-optimality",
      "Iteration 2 pivot: entering $x_2$, leaving $s_2$ with pivot element $4/3$ and minimum ratio $1.5$",
      "Final tableau verification: all reduced costs in the $z$-row non-negative ($s_1$-coeff $= 3/4$, $s_2$-coeff $= 1/2$)",
      "Direct extraction of final optimal solution: $x_1^* = 3$, $x_2^* = 1.5$, and maximal profit $z^* = 21$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "title": "Post-Optimal Resource Classification: Scarce Versus Abundant Constraints",
    "scope": "Defines the economic and physical interpretation of optimal slack values. Teaches how to categorize operational resources and constraints into scarce versus abundant based on whether slack variables are fully depleted or retain positive residual capacity.",
    "key_points": [
      "Definition of a scarce resource: an input whose associated slack variable equals zero ($s_i^* = 0$) at optimality",
      "Physical meaning of scarce resources: inputs that are fully exhausted by optimal operational activities, acting as binding constraints",
      "Definition of an abundant resource: an input whose associated slack variable is strictly positive ($s_i^* > 0$) at optimality",
      "Physical meaning of abundant resources: non-binding constraints with unused slack capacity (slack margins)",
      "Constraint analysis of the Tatar-Paint system: classification of raw materials M1 and M2 as scarce versus market and demand limits as abundant"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "title": "Generalization of the Simplex Framework and Starting Solution Prerequisites",
    "scope": "Synthesizes the core rules of the simplex algorithm across general optimization directions and establishes the requirement for artificial starting solutions when the natural origin is infeasible.",
    "key_points": [
      "Unified summary of the Simplex Optimality Condition for both maximization and minimization objectives",
      "Universal validity of the Simplex Feasibility Condition (minimum ratio test with positive denominator) regardless of objective direction",
      "Assumption of initial feasibility: requirement that the origin ($x = 0$) satisfies all constraints ($b_i \\ge 0$ with all $\\le$ inequalities)",
      "Failure of standard origin initialization in the presence of $\\ge$ or $=$ constraints (infeasible origin)",
      "Conceptual introduction to artificial variables and starting solution techniques (Two-Phase and Big-M methods) to initialize non-origin bases"
    ]
  }
]
